content:
alex: Quick proposal — rethink telemetry indexing to reduce dashboard P99s. Current model: single composite PK on (route_id, event_time) + JSONb attributes. Scans when users filter on high-card attributes = CPU spikes.

alex: I sketched two approaches:
1) attribute inverted index (posting lists per attr:value) + small doc store for event metadata — fast filtering, slower writes and storage blowup.
2) denormalized materialized 'route_profile_metrics' table (pre-aggregated dims) — very fast dashboard queries, but more upfront ETL/backfill and less ad-hoc flexibility.

maria: +1 on exploring inverted index for only high-card filterable attrs. Storage will grow but we can TTL cold postings. Need rough cost estimate though. :money_with_wings:

jon: Concern: backfill duration and burst writes. If we dual-write from API -> both index and current table we avoid long-lived backfills, but queries will see mixed coverage until backfill completes. That's rough for SLAs.

priya: Query patterns from console: most dashboards filter by {route_tag, env, model_family} and free-text search on route name. That suggests we should index route_tag and model_family first. Route name search might be a small trigram index or use prefix index on a separate search table.

alex: Agreed. Proposal tweak: inverted index for route_tag & model_family + lightweight trigram for route name. Materialized table for time-windowed aggregates (1min/5min) used by charts. Dual-write for 48h + backfill for last 90d.

lisa: How do we measure effectiveness? We should add a dashboard with: index hit ratio, avg query scan bytes, write amplification, backfill progress. Also track costs daily.

maria: Can we TTL posting lists older than 180d but keep aggregates? That would reduce cold storage. Also consider compression (zstd) for postings.

jon: Rollout plan sketch:
- stage: deploy inverted index service in staging with shadow write for 24h
- canary: route small % of console traffic (5%) to new query path
- backfill: parallel workers with throughput cap, monitor replication lag
- cutoff: switch reads when index coverage > 95% for last 30d

alex: Example query glue (pseudo):
```
-- find candidate route_ids
SELECT route_id FROM attr_index WHERE attr='model_family' AND value='llama';
-- join with aggregates for timeseries
SELECT ts, sum(tokens) FROM route_agg WHERE route_id IN (..candidate ids..) GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts;
```

priya: Nice. For the attr_index schema, consider sharding by hash(attr,value) and store postings as compressed arrays to reduce read IO. Also add a small bloom filter per shard to skip empty lookups in many queries.

ingest-bot: Note: deploy pipeline will create a new k8s StatefulSet for posting-list workers. Will emit events to #eng-infra when stage deploy starts.

lisa: One more: retention & compliance — if customers request purges, we need per-tenant tombstones in both postings and aggregates. Make sure dual-write respects deletion semantics.

maria: ops question — does current tracing capture query plan distributions? We should emit histogram of scanned_bytes per query so we can verify improvement post-rollout.

alex: Next steps I've captured: (1) run cost estimate for inverted posting lists vs materialized storage for 90d window (2) prototype posting-list storage + compression & bloom filter (3) define canary/read-cutover signals and dashboards (4) doc the dual-write/backfill safety checklist.

jon: I'll volunteer to own the canary signals and rollback playbook.

maria: I'll coordinate cost calc and retention implications with finance/compliance.

priya: I'll prototype the shard + bloom filter layout, share a quick perf harness next week.

alex: Great — syncing tomorrow 10:30 to align PRs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
